response.reasoning:
Both sides agree the parcel arrived and that one of the four set boxes has a crushed, split corner. What separates them is when that happened. The photograph of the outer shipping carton shows it square, sealed and undamaged, with no crushing or impact mark on any corner, and marked fragile. It is hard to see how a box inside could be crushed hard enough to split open while the carton around it stayed in that condition. The photograph of the set itself shows a corner that is torn and pushed in, along with general rubbing along the edges. On the balance of what is in front of me, the damage was more likely present before posting than caused in transit, so the seller carries it rather than the carrier.

That matters here more than it usually would, because the buyer asked directly, before buying, whether the boxes were in good condition and said that for a retired set the box is most of what they were paying for. The seller answered that the boxes were fine and the listing said the same. So this is not a small unmentioned flaw; it goes to the exact point the buyer checked.

Against that, the loss is partial. Four sets were bought and only one box is affected; the other three are not said to be faulty, and nothing suggests any of the contents are missing or damaged. The buyer keeps everything. The fair measure is the drop in value of the one damaged set, weighted up because the condition of the box was the thing specifically promised, not the whole price. A share of thirty per cent of the money being held to the buyer reflects that: real compensation for a set whose box no longer matches what was described, while the seller keeps the value of what was delivered as promised.

findings.statement: Before buying, the buyer asked specifically about box condition and said it was most of what they were paying for; the seller replied that the boxes were fine, and the listing described them as in good condition.
The parcel was posted on 26 August and delivered on 28 August, and the buyer said something was wrong the same day it arrived.
The photograph of the outer shipping carton shows it intact, sealed and square, with no crushing or impact damage to any corner.
The photograph of the set shows a torn and pushed-in corner on the box, together with edge wear, which is inconsistent with a box described as like new and in good condition.
An undamaged outer carton alongside a split corner on the item inside points to the damage existing before posting rather than being caused in transit, contrary to the seller's account.
Only one of the four sets is said to be affected, and no missing or damaged contents are alleged.
The concern was raised within the time allowed after the purchase was completed.
